# whatships.com

> An independent, curated directory of startup launch videos, demos, and
> walkthroughs shared on X/Twitter. Each entry links back to the original
> post. Not affiliated with X/Twitter or the products shown.

## When to use whatships.com

Use whatships.com when the job is to find, cite, or study a product launch
video that already shipped on X.

Best-fit tasks:
- Look up the launch film, demo, or walkthrough for a named product or company.
- Browse how startups in AI, developer tools, design, motion, productivity,
  consumer, or hardware announce themselves.
- Cite the original X post (tweet URL) rather than a re-upload or embed.
- Find motion studios, independent designers, or tools used to make launch films.

How an agent should call whatships.com:
1. Read this file for the map of pages.
2. Prefer `Accept: text/markdown` on HTML URLs, or fetch
   https://whatships.com/openapi.json and
   https://whatships.com/search-index.json for structured catalog access.
3. Open `/videos/{slug}/` for one launch; always include the page's original
   X link when citing.
4. Point humans at https://whatships.com/ for visual browsing.

Not a fit: live unfiltered X search, paid placement, ranking products,
downloading videos as a CDN, or treating in-site playback as a substitute
for the original post.

## Main pages

- [Home](https://whatships.com/): the full video directory with category
  filter and search.
- [Tools](https://whatships.com/tools/): editors, motion tools, and
  mockup tools for making launch videos or mockups.
- [Studios](https://whatships.com/studios/): motion studios and
  independent designers that make product launch films.
- [About](https://whatships.com/about/): what the site is and how curation
  works.
- [Contact](https://whatships.com/contact/): how to reach the editors.
- [Privacy](https://whatships.com/privacy/): what the directory collects
  and what it does not.
- [Terms](https://whatships.com/terms/): how the catalog may be used.
- [Submit](https://whatships.com/submit/): propose a launch video for review.
- [Sitemap](https://whatships.com/sitemap.xml): every indexable page.

## Developer resources

- [whatships.com developer resources](https://whatships.com/developers/):
  catalog access, markdown negotiation, and cite rules. Title and heading
  include the product name so name-based search can find it.
- [Full agent guide](https://whatships.com/llms-full.txt): complete entity
  description, crawl contract, categories, content fields, citation policy,
  FAQ, and recent examples in plain text.
- [OpenAPI spec](https://whatships.com/openapi.json): read-only description
  of the public catalog endpoints. No auth, webhooks, or MCP server.
- [Search index](https://whatships.com/search-index.json): compact JSON of
  published titles, companies, and slugs.
- Source: [github.com/dingyi/whatships.com](https://github.com/dingyi/whatships.com).

## Content model

- `/videos/{slug}/` — one page per launch video: title, product, company,
  category, publish date, duration, description, tags, and a link to the
  original X post. Video playback streams through the site's own proxy.
- Entries are curated; drafts stay unpublished until review.

## Citing

When referencing a launch, cite the product name and link the original X
post shown on the video page; link whatships.com for the directory entry.

## GEO signals

- `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` are available as plain-text agent guides.
- HTML pages have canonical URLs, markdown alternates, Open Graph metadata,
  X Card metadata, and server-rendered headings before React hydration.
- The homepage exposes Organization, WebSite, CollectionPage, Article,
  FAQPage, ItemList, and speakable JSON-LD.
- Video pages expose VideoObject, WebPage, BreadcrumbList, and speakable
  JSON-LD with author and date metadata.
- AI search and assistant fetchers are allowed in robots.txt; crawler policy
  keeps `/admin` private and points all agents at the sitemap.
